NONE: A1 being the first one after the present one or after the one just mentioned
下一個的；其次的；緊接著的
A2 immediately after
接下來，然後
B1 The time when you next do something is the first time you do it again
下次
A2 used when describing two people or things that are very close to each other with nothing between them
緊靠著，緊挨著
› used to mean `after' when making a choice or a comparison
（用於作出選擇或比較時）僅次於，在…之後
› almost
幾乎
› next in order to appear or happen, often in some form of entertainment
（常指娛樂節目）接下來

example: Who works in the office next to yours?
誰在你隔壁的辦公室工作？
Take the next street on the right.
在下一個路口右轉。
Who do you think will be the next president?
你認為誰會出任下屆總統？
Nothing really changes around here. One day is pretty much like the next.
這裡並沒有甚麼實質變化，天天差不多都是一樣。
(The) next time you want to borrow something, please ask me first.
下次你想借東西的話，請先問問我。
I'm so busy it's hard to remember what I'm supposed to be doing from one minute to the next.
我忙得經常記不清下一步該做甚麼。
She's away for the next few days.
她未來數天休假。
You'll have to wait until your next birthday for a new bike.
你要等到下一個生日才會收到新腳踏車。
Can we arrange a meeting for the week after next?
我們安排兩星期後開會，可以嗎？
What do you think you'll be doing this time next year?
你認為明年這個時候自己會在做甚麼？
We had a big argument, but he called me the next day (= the day after) to apologize.
我們發生了激烈的爭吵，不過第二天他就打電話向我道歉了。
Excuse me, it's my turn - I was next.
對不起，輪到我了——我是下一個。
So what happened next?
那後來怎麼樣了？
What would you like next?
你還喜歡甚麼？
First, fry the garlic. Next, add the ginger.
先炒一下大蒜，再加生薑。
[ + -ing verb ] When are you next going to Toronto?
你下次甚麼時候去多倫多？
Can I sit next to the window?
我可以靠窗坐嗎？
There was a really strange man standing next to me at the train station.
在車站有一個很古怪的男人站在我旁邊。
Cheese is my favourite food and, next to that, chocolate. (= Cheese is the only food that I like more than chocolate.)
起司是我最喜歡的食品，其次是巧克力。
They pay me next to nothing (= very little) but I really enjoy the work.
他們沒付給我多少錢，但我實在喜歡那工作。
It's next to impossible (= extremely difficult) to find somewhere cheap to live around here.
要在這附近找到廉價的住處極其困難。
We got home in next to no time (= very little time).
我們很快就到家了。

NONE: › the person or group of people you are most closely related to
直系親屬

example: We cannot release the names of the soldiers who were killed until we have informed their next of kin.
遇害士兵的姓名要待我們通知其直系親屬之後才能公佈。

NONE: › The next to last person or thing is the one before the last one.
倒數第二的

example: I was next to last in the race.
我在賽跑中排名倒數第二。
He injured himself on the next-to-last day of his vacation.
他在假期結束前一天受傷了。

NONE: › best except for another thing that has been mentioned
僅次於…的；退而求其次的

example: If you can't afford to fly to the Caribbean, this restaurant is the next-best thing.
如果你沒錢飛去加勒比地區的話，那麼這家餐館就是最好的選擇。
The best performing sector was construction, and the next-best performers were transportation and retail.
表現最好的行業是建築，其次是交通和零售。

NONE: › used to refer to something that will happen or be done on the next day
第二天的，隔日的

example: Standard next-day delivery of your order is included.
標準的隔日投遞服務已包括在你的訂單中。
It's not always easy to get a next-day appointment.
能約到第二天不是很容易。
We booked a next-day flight to Miami.
我們訂了第二天去邁阿密的機票。

NONE: › an important connection between the parts of a system or a group of things
（重要的）連接，聯繫

example: Times Square is the nexus of the New York subway.
時代廣場是紐約地鐵的交會點。
